# Reliability and code quality: build rules

Apply these rules while you build. Domains or criteria whose `applies_if` flags are false in `.quality/project.json` do not apply to this project. Before you call a task done, check your work against the criteria of the domains you touched: each one must be true and verifiable.

If a stack module of the quality pack is installed (qp-nextjs, qp-node-api, qp-vps, qp-expo, qp-capacitor), its rules skill adds stack-specific rules on top of these.

## Reliability (REL)

Errors, interruptions and edge cases.

Rules:

- Every network call has a timeout, error handling and, if idempotent, limited retries.
- Plan edge cases in the spec: empty list, very long list, special characters, double click, expired session, network loss.
- An error in one component does not take down the whole page (error boundary or equivalent).
- The server shuts down cleanly: it finishes in-flight requests and closes its connections.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] REL-01: No unhandled error that crashes the server or the app. Check: Search for promises without catch, handlers without try/catch, missing error boundaries.
- [major] REL-02: Timeouts and failure handling on all external calls. Check: fetch, HTTP clients, database, Redis: timeout and failure behaviour.
- [major] REL-03: Double submit and concurrent requests without side effects. Check: Double click on payment, sign-up, create: a single result (idempotency or lock).
- [major] REL-04: Correct behaviour offline, on slow network and after session expiry (only if: has_ui). Check: Cut the network, throttle, expire the session mid-flow.
- [minor] REL-05: Extreme inputs handled (empty, very long, emoji, special characters). Check: Enter these values in each field and check display and storage.
- [minor] REL-06: Clean server shutdown (SIGTERM handled) (only if: has_backend). Check: Read the entry point: closing of the HTTP server, sockets and connections.

## Tests (TST)

Validation and regression prevention.

Rules:

- Any logic with a branch, loop, money calculation, parsing or security comes with at least one test.
- Every fixed bug gets a test that would have caught it.
- Main flows have an end-to-end test that runs in CI.
- Never declare a task done without running the tests and reading their output.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] TST-01: The test suite passes entirely. Check: Run the project's test command; no test skipped without a written reason.
- [major] TST-02: Risky logic is tested (money, permissions, calculations, parsing). Check: List these functions and check a test covers them.
- [major] TST-03: Main flows have an end-to-end test (only if: has_ui). Check: Playwright (or Detox, Maestro on mobile) tests for each main flow.
- [major] TST-04: Tests run automatically before every production release. Check: CI pipeline that blocks deployment when a test fails.
- [minor] TST-05: Tests check behaviour, not implementation. Check: No tests that merely mirror the code or mock everything.

## Code (COD)

Maintainability, typing, linting, no console errors and no leftover debug logs.

Rules:

- The simplest code that fully solves the problem: no unrequested abstraction, option or configuration.
- Reuse what exists in the project before adding a dependency or a helper.
- Change only what the task requires; flag the rest instead of rewriting it.
- Strict typing, no unjustified any; automatic lint and format before each commit.
- No debug console.log, commented-out code or temporary file left behind.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] COD-01: No type or build error. Check: The stack module's typecheck and build commands.
- [major] COD-02: No lint error. Check: The stack module's lint command.
- [major] COD-03: No error or warning in the browser console (only if: has_ui). Check: Open each main page with Playwright and collect the console.
- [major] COD-04: No debug log, commented-out code or temporary file. Check: Search for console.log, debugger, large commented blocks, *.bak, *.tmp files.
- [minor] COD-05: Strict typing and justified any. Check: strict enabled; every any or ts-ignore has an explaining comment.
- [minor] COD-06: No over-engineering or duplication. Check: Single-use abstractions, unused options, copy-pasted functions.
- [minor] COD-07: Up-to-date README: install, run, environment variables. Check: Follow the README on a clean machine; complete .env.example.
